overview.intro:
Chapter 73 covers articles made of iron or steel: sheet piling and railway track material (7301–7302); cast-iron, seamless and welded pipe and tube (7303–7306); pipe fittings (7307); structures such as towers, bridges, doors and scaffolding (7308); tanks, drums, cans and gas cylinders (7309–7311); wire rope, mesh, fencing, chain and anchors (7312–7316); nails, screws, bolts and nuts (7317–7318); needles and springs (7319–7320); stoves, grills and radiators (7321–7322); kitchenware and sanitary ware (7323–7324); and other cast, forged and wire articles (7325–7326). **446 of the 573 tariff lines are Free** under the general rate; the rest pay 1.5% to 12.5%, mostly fittings, fasteners, springs and household articles.

What decides the cost is **Section 232**, charged on the **full customs value** since April 6, 2026. **495 lines pay 50%** (heading 9903.82.02): all pipe and tube, sheet piling and rails, fittings, structures, containers, wire products, chain, nails, fasteners, springs and most cast and other articles. **64 household lines pay 25%** (9903.82.09): stoves, ranges and grills, radiators and air heaters, kitchenware, sinks and other sanitary ware, and some wire and other articles. Both apply to every country, on top of any FTA or USMCA rate. Lower rates exist only for UK steel (25% or 15%), for derivative articles made from at least 85% U.S.-melted steel (10%), and for limited Commerce-authorized Canadian or Mexican pipe and tube (25%). **Only 14 cast-iron lines** (cast-iron pipe, nonmalleable cast fittings, cast-iron radiators, cookware and baths) are outside Section 232; they pay the 2026 Section 301 duties instead.

China pays **Section 301** on top, so Chinese pipe, nails, bolts and structures pay **75%**. Canadian steel structures of 7308.90 pay **100%** since September 15, 2026 (Section 338 plus Section 232). Leaf and coil springs for vehicles pay the Section 232 auto or truck parts duty instead of the metals duty. Many Chapter 73 products also carry company-specific **antidumping and countervailing duties** (oil country tubular goods, line and standard pipe, rectangular tube, fittings, nails, threaded rod, wind towers, PC strand, propane cylinders, sinks, garment hangers); they are not part of this table or the tariff calculator.

productGroups.label: Sheet piling & welded shapes
productGroups.blurb: Steel sheet piling and welded angles, shapes and sections: 3 lines, all Free. All pay the 50% Section 232 duty (sheet piling as a steel article since 2018, welded shapes as derivatives since March 12, 2025).

productGroups.label: Railway track material
productGroups.blurb: Rails, switch blades, crossing frogs, fish-plates, sole plates, sleepers and rail clips: 15 lines, all Free. All pay the 50% Section 232 duty; Chinese rails also 25% Section 301 (note 31).

productGroups.label: Cast-iron pipe & tube
productGroups.blurb: Cast-iron soil pipe, pressure pipe and other cast-iron tubes: 3 lines, all Free. Outside Section 232; they pay the 2026 Section 301 duties (10% or 12.5%) unless USMCA is claimed. Chinese soil pipe carries AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Seamless pipe & tube (OCTG, line pipe)
productGroups.blurb: Seamless line pipe, drill pipe, casing and tubing (OCTG), boiler tubes and mechanical tubing: 139 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232 from every country; 75% from China. Seamless OCTG and standard pipe carry AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Large welded pipe (over 406.4 mm)
productGroups.blurb: Welded pipe with an outside diameter over 406.4 mm (large-diameter line pipe, casing): 21 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232; large-diameter welded pipe from six countries and line pipe from Japan carry AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Welded pipe & tube
productGroups.blurb: Welded line pipe, OCTG, standard and structural pipe, stainless tube and square or rectangular tube: 68 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232; many products carry AD/CVD orders (standard pipe, rectangular tube, stainless pressure pipe).

productGroups.label: Pipe fittings & flanges
productGroups.blurb: Cast, forged and butt-welding fittings, flanges, elbows and couplings: 39 lines, mostly 3.2% to 6.2%. 50% Section 232 except the 3 nonmalleable cast-iron fittings (7307.11), which pay the 2026 Section 301 duties instead.

productGroups.label: Structures & parts (towers, bridges, doors)
productGroups.blurb: Bridges, towers and lattice masts (including wind towers), doors and windows, scaffolding, grating and other structural parts: 15 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232; Canadian 7308.90 structures pay another 50% (Section 338).

productGroups.label: Tanks & vats over 300 liters
productGroups.blurb: Reservoirs, tanks and vats over 300 liters: 2 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232 on the full value.

productGroups.label: Drums, cans & boxes up to 300 liters
productGroups.blurb: Drums, kegs, cans and boxes up to 300 liters, including aerosol cans: 10 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Gas cylinders
productGroups.blurb: Cylinders and other containers for compressed or liquefied gas: 3 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232; steel propane cylinders from China and Thailand carry AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Wire rope, cable & strand
productGroups.blurb: Stranded wire, wire rope, cables, slings and PC strand: 23 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232; PC strand from many countries carries AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Barbed wire
productGroups.blurb: Barbed wire and twisted fencing wire: 1 line, Free. 50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Wire cloth, mesh & fencing
productGroups.blurb: Woven wire cloth, chain-link, welded wire mesh, fencing and expanded metal: 25 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Chain
productGroups.blurb: Roller chain, link chain, skid chain and chain parts: 20 lines, mostly Free (3 dutiable at 1.5% to 3.9%). 50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Anchors & grapnels
productGroups.blurb: Anchors and grapnels: 1 line, Free. 50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Nails, tacks & staples
productGroups.blurb: Nails, tacks, staples and similar articles: 23 lines, all Free. 50% Section 232 (some nails since 2020); 75% from China. Nails from China, Korea, Malaysia, Oman, Taiwan, Vietnam and the UAE carry AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Screws, bolts, nuts & washers
productGroups.blurb: Screws, bolts, nuts, washers, studs, rivets and threaded rod: 48 lines, Free to 12.5%. 50% Section 232 on all; 75% from China. Threaded rod from China, India, Taiwan and Thailand carries AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Needles & pins
productGroups.blurb: Sewing needles, knitting needles, safety pins and other pins: 7 lines, Free to 4.5%. 50% Section 232.

productGroups.label: Springs
productGroups.blurb: Leaf springs, coil springs, hairsprings and other springs: 14 lines, Free to 3.9%. 50% Section 232, except leaf and coil springs for vehicles, which pay the Section 232 auto or truck parts duty instead.

productGroups.label: Stoves, ranges & grills
productGroups.blurb: Gas ranges, stoves, barbecue grills, fireplaces, heaters and their parts: 24 lines, mostly Free (4 lines at 2.9% or 5.7%). 25% Section 232 (list (vii)), on top of USMCA; 50% from China on most lines.

productGroups.label: Radiators & air heaters
productGroups.blurb: Central-heating radiators, air heaters and hot-air distributors: 5 lines, all Free. 25% Section 232 except cast-iron radiators (7322.11), which are outside it.

productGroups.label: Kitchen & household articles
productGroups.blurb: Cookware, kitchenware, tableware, steel wool and other household articles: 25 lines, Free to 8.2%. 25% Section 232 on 20 lines; cast-iron cookware (7323.91, 7323.92) is outside Section 232. Chinese stainless cookware pays no Section 301.

productGroups.label: Sinks & sanitary ware
productGroups.blurb: Stainless steel sinks and wash basins, baths and other sanitary ware: 6 lines, Free or 3.4%. 25% Section 232 except cast-iron baths (7324.21). Drawn stainless sinks from China carry AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Cast articles (manhole covers, grinding balls)
productGroups.blurb: Manhole covers, catch basins, meter boxes, grinding balls and other cast articles: 9 lines, Free or 2.9%. 50% Section 232 (25% for meter boxes); the nonmalleable cast-iron lines (7325.10) were added on April 6, 2026.

productGroups.label: Other articles (forged, wire, hangers)
productGroups.blurb: Forged and stamped articles, wire articles (garment hangers, belting), ladders, fence posts, caskets and other steel articles: 24 lines, Free to 8.6%. 50% Section 232 on 13 lines, 25% on 11.

workedExamples.title: $500,000 of steel bolts from Taiwan
workedExamples.body: Bolts of this line are **Free** under the general rate, but they are Section 232 derivative steel articles (note 16(c)(iv)), so they pay **+50% of the full value** (9903.82.02): **$250,000**. Taiwan's 2026 Section 301 rate does not apply to Section 232 goods (note 52(f)(1)). Threaded rod (7318.15.50) from Taiwan is also under an antidumping order.

workedExamples.title: Steel structural parts from Canada, with a USMCA certification
workedExamples.body: USMCA makes the base rate Free, but note 16(b) collects Section 232 on top: **+50%** (9903.82.02). This line is also on the Section 338 list for Canada (note 51(b)(3)), and since **September 15, 2026** that **+50%** (9903.03.14) is charged in addition to Section 232: **100%** of the value, USMCA or not.

workedExamples.title: A gas range from Mexico, USMCA-qualifying
workedExamples.body: Free under the general rate and under USMCA, but stoves and ranges are on Section 232 list (vii): **+25%** (9903.82.09) on the full value, so $25,000 on a $100,000 shipment. If at least 85% of the steel was melted and poured in the United States the rate is **10%** (9903.82.06). The 2026 Section 301 duty does not apply.

workedExamples.title: Seamless OCTG casing from South Korea
workedExamples.body: Free at base, **+50%** Section 232 (9903.82.02): $50,000 on $100,000. KORUS does not reduce it. Seamless and welded oil country tubular goods from Korea are also under an antidumping order (sunset review completed January 2026), so a company-specific cash deposit comes on top.

Stainless household articles of 7323.93 were on Section 301 List 4B, which never took effect, so there is no Section 301 duty, and the 2026 Section 301 duty on China does not apply to Section 232 goods. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.

workedExamples.title: Cast-iron soil pipe from Mexico or China
workedExamples.body: Cast-iron pipe is **not** on the Section 232 lists. From Mexico it is **Free** with a USMCA claim and **10%** without one (2026 Section 301, 9903.05.55). From China: **25%** Section 301 List 3 plus **12.5%** (9903.05.31) = **37.5%**, plus the antidumping and countervailing duties on cast-iron soil pipe from China.

workedExamples.title: Leaf springs for cars from Japan
workedExamples.body: A passenger-vehicle part pays the Section 232 **auto parts** duty instead of the metals duty. For Japan the total is **15%** (9903.94.43) in place of the 3.2% base rate. The same spring not used in a vehicle would pay 3.2% + 50% = 53.2%.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule, the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026), and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 73 today. Base rates did not change: 567 of 573 lines are the same, and six statistical lines were added by splitting existing ones (electrical conduit in 7306.30.10, wind turbine towers in 7308.20.00, aerosol cans in 7310.21.00) at the same Free rate.

The extra duties changed a lot. In January 2025, Section 232 reached only pipe and tube, sheet piling, rails and certain nails, at 25%, with Canada, Mexico and others exempt or under quotas. Proclamation 10896 ended every exemption and added **almost all other Chapter 73 articles as steel derivatives on March 12, 2025**; Proclamation 10947 raised the rate to **50% on June 4, 2025**; and Proclamation 11021 rebuilt the program on **April 6, 2026**: **50%** (9903.82.02) on 495 lines and **25%** (9903.82.09) on 64 household lines, both on the **full customs value**. The IEEPA duties never added to Section 232 goods after June 4, 2025 and **ended on February 24, 2026**; the Section 122 surcharge and the 2026 Section 301 duties also leave Section 232 goods alone. China's Section 301 duties do stack, and Canada's Section 338 duty stacks on 7308.90 structures.

Antidumping and countervailing duty orders cover many pipe, fitting, fastener and wire products. They are company-specific, listed below for reference, and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 73 from any country: Section 232 metals (note 16), the Section 232 auto parts and medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts duties on vehicle springs (notes 33, 38), China Section 301 (notes 20, 31), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50, 52), Canada Section 338 (note 51), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua Section 301 duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. The main antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chapter 73 products are listed for reference; the calculator does not model them. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.country: All countries (Canada, Mexico, EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, India and Vietnam included)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 steel articles and derivatives, on the full customs value
inEffect.before: +25% on pipe and tube, sheet piling, rails and certain nails only, with Canada, Mexico, Argentina, Australia, Brazil and Korea exempt or under quotas and the EU, Japan and UK under tariff-rate quotas
inEffect.exemption: Covers 495 lines. List (iii), steel articles: sheet piling (7301.10), rails and track material (7302.10, 7302.40, 7302.90) and all pipe and tube of 7304–7306. List (iv), derivative steel articles: welded shapes (7301.20), switch blades and frogs (7302.30), fittings (7307, except nonmalleable cast fittings), structures (7308), tanks, drums and gas cylinders (7309–7311), wire rope, barbed wire, mesh, chain and anchors (7312–7316), nails (7317), fasteners (7318), needles and pins (7319), springs (7320), most cast articles (7325) and 13 lines of 7326. No country exemptions, quotas or product exclusions. Note 16(b): collected on top of any FTA or USMCA rate. Lower rates: UK steel at least 95% UK-melted (9903.82.04, 25%); derivatives with at least 85% U.S.-melted steel (9903.82.06, 10%); limited Commerce-authorized Canadian or Mexican pipe and tube (9903.82.18, 25%). Russia uses 9903.82.14 (also 50%). Goods under 9903.82.02 do not pay the 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duties (notes 52(f)(1), 50(a)(vi)(1)). Vehicle springs pay the auto or truck parts duty instead.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Pipe, fittings, fasteners, nails and structures pay half their value again in duty: $400,000 of welded pipe or bolts from any country owes $200,000 plus any base rate.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 derivative steel articles of list (vii), on the full customs value
inEffect.before: None (not on the Section 232 lists before March 12, 2025)
inEffect.exemption: Covers 64 lines: stoves, ranges, grills and their parts (7321), radiators other than cast iron and air heaters (7322.19, 7322.90), household articles other than cast iron (7323.10, 7323.93, 7323.94, 7323.99), stainless sinks and other sanitary ware other than cast-iron baths (7324.10, 7324.29, 7324.90), meter boxes (7325.10.00.35), wire articles such as belting, garment hangers and ties (7326.20.00.10–.55), and pocket containers, horseshoes, ladders, paint roller frames, broom handles and caskets (7326.90). They paid 25% from March 12, 2025 and 50% from June 4, 2025 under Proclamations 10896 and 10947; Proclamation 11021 set 25% from April 6, 2026. UK products with at least 95% UK-melted steel pay 15% (9903.82.05); at least 85% U.S.-melted steel, 10% (9903.82.06); Russia uses 9903.82.16 (25%). Manufacturing drawback is allowed for these lines when they are products of the UK, EU, Japan, Korea, Mexico or Canada made from steel melted and poured there and not of a kind under an AD/CVD order (Proclamation 11021 clause 13).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $100,000 container of gas ranges, grills or stainless cookware pays $25,000 of Section 232 duty, USMCA or not.

inEffect.before: Tariff-rate quota for UK steel articles (Free in quota, +25% over); UK nails exempt
inEffect.exemption: Note 16(d): only when at least 95% of the steel was melted and poured in the United Kingdom; Commerce (91 FR 23056) lets Tata Steel UK steel melted and poured in the Netherlands count as UK until January 1, 2028. UK goods that do not meet the test pay 50% (9903.82.02) or 25% (9903.82.09). The UK's 10% 2026 Section 301 rate (9903.05.81) applies only to the 14 cast-iron lines; UK vehicle springs pay 10% under the UK auto parts quota heading (9903.94.32).
inEffect.whatItMeans: UK-melted steel pipe or fittings ship at half the duty of other countries: $100,000 pays $25,000 instead of $50,000.

inEffect.measure: Section 301: note 31 (2024 review), Lists 2, 3 and 4A, and the 2026 action
inEffect.now: +25% or +7.5% on top of Section 232 (75% on pipe, tube, nails, bolts and structures); +12.5% only on the 14 non-Section 232 lines
inEffect.exemption: Note 31 (9903.91.01) charges 25% on 234 lines, the pipe, tube, rails and sheet piling of 79 Chapter 73 subheadings, since September 27, 2024. List 2 (9903.88.02) covers structures of 7308 (10 lines), List 3 (9903.88.03) 269 lines, List 4A (9903.88.15, 7.5%) 43 lines (some cold-drawn tube, nails, fasteners, springs, stoves, kitchenware, sanitary ware). 17 household lines pay none of these: stainless cookware (7323.93) and some other kitchenware and stoves, which are on the suspended List 4B, and unenameled cast-iron cookware (7323.91.50). All of these stack with Section 232. The 12.5% 2026 duty on China (9903.05.31) applies only to the 14 cast-iron lines outside Section 232. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue during the four-year review. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese pipe, nails, bolts and structures pay 75% of their value; Chinese gas grills 50%; Chinese stainless cookware 27%.

inEffect.country: All countries (Japan, EU, Korea and Taiwan 15% total; UK 10%)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 automobile parts and medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts (vehicle springs)
inEffect.now: +25% in place of the metals duty (Japan, EU, Korea, Taiwan: 15% in place of the base rate; UK: 10%)
inEffect.exemption: Six spring lines (leaf springs of 7320.10 and suspension coil springs 7320.20.10) are on the auto parts list (note 33) and the truck parts list (note 38). When they are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks they pay the auto parts duty (9903.94.05, 25%, from May 3, 2025; Japan 9903.94.43, EU 9903.94.53, Korea 9903.94.63 and Taiwan 9903.94.67 at 15% in place of the base rate; UK 9903.94.32 at 10%); as parts of medium- or heavy-duty trucks or buses, 25% (9903.74.08) from November 1, 2025. Either way the metals duty does not also apply. USMCA-qualifying parts of Canada or Mexico pay no auto parts duty (9903.94.06) or truck parts duty (9903.74.10). Springs not for vehicles pay the 50% metals duty.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Leaf springs for a pickup truck from India pay 3.2% + 25% = 28.2%; the same springs from Japan pay 15%; from Mexico with USMCA, nothing.

inEffect.country: 60 Section 301 economies (Canada, Mexico, EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Thailand, UK, Russia and others)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5% (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan: 10% or 12.5% in place of the base rate) on the 14 non-Section 232 lines
inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 goods (note 52(f)(1), 9903.05.90), so it reaches only cast-iron pipe (7303), nonmalleable cast fittings (7307.11), cast-iron radiators (7322.11), cast-iron cookware (7323.91, 7323.92) and cast-iron baths (7324.21). USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Only cast-iron goods pay it: $100,000 of Indian cast-iron fittings (7307.11) pays 4.8% + 10% = $14,800.

inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 goods (note 50(a)(vi)(1), 9903.05.07), so Brazilian pipe, fittings and fasteners pay only Section 232. The 14 cast-iron lines pay 25% (9903.05.01) and 12.5% (9903.05.27).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian steel pipe pays 50%; Brazilian cast-iron soil pipe pays 37.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Charged even when USMCA is claimed. Since September 15, 2026 (Proclamation 11065) it applies in addition to Section 232, so these structural parts, roofing, siding and architectural work of Canada pay 50% + 50%. Civil aircraft articles are exempt (9903.03.16). No other Chapter 73 line is on the list.
inEffect.whatItMeans: $200,000 of Canadian steel structural parts pays $200,000 of duty.

inEffect.before: 70% in place of column 2 on 130 lines, +25% Section 232 on pipe and tube
inEffect.now: Column 2 rate, or 70% in its place on 130 lines, plus 50% (9903.82.14) or 25% (9903.82.16) Section 232
inEffect.exemption: Russia has paid column 2 rates since April 9, 2022, and 70% in lieu of column 2 on the note 30(d) metal subheadings (130 Chapter 73 lines: much of the pipe and tube, some fittings, structures, containers, fasteners and cast articles) since April 1, 2023 (Proclamation 10523). One aluminum-derivative line (7308.20.00.35, wind towers) pays 200% if it is a Russian aluminum article (9903.85.68). The 14 cast-iron lines pay 12.5% under Section 301 (9903.05.66). U.S. imports from Russia were under $0.1 million in 2025.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian seamless pipe on a note 30(d) line pays 70% + 50% = 120% of its value.

changes.title: No Chapter 73 base-rate changes
changes.detail: 567 of 573 Chapter 73 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. Six statistical lines were added by splitting existing ones, all Free: 7306.30.10.10 (welded tube lined for electrical conduit) and .90; 7308.20.00.30 (tubular towers) and .35 (tubular wind turbine towers); 7310.21.00.70 (aerosol cans up to 11.4 liters) and .75.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29). Note 29 has no Section 232 carve-out, so it will add to Section 232 on Nicaraguan steel articles. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Garment hangers finished in Cambodia: preliminary circumvention finding
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found that steel wire garment hangers (7326.20.00.20) completed in Cambodia from Chinese or Vietnamese wire circumvent the antidumping order on China and the AD/CVD orders on Vietnam. The China order was continued in February 2025.

changes.title: Section 338 duty on Canadian steel structures stacks on Section 232
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on products of Canada in the note 51(b)(3) list, which includes the structural parts, roofing, siding and architectural work of 7308.90.30, 7308.90.60 and 7308.90.95; it is charged even on USMCA goods. The duty started August 22, 2026 (Proclamation 11056), and from September 15, 2026 it applies in addition to Section 232 (Proclamation 11065), so these goods pay 100%.

changes.title: Steel nails: Commerce sunset findings on five countries
changes.detail: In expedited second sunset reviews, Commerce found that revoking the antidumping orders on steel nails from Korea, Malaysia, Oman, Taiwan and Vietnam would likely lead to continued dumping; the orders stay in place pending the ITC's review. The order on nails from China was continued May 1, 2025.
changes.countries: Korea, Malaysia, Oman, Taiwan, Vietnam, China

changes.title: Light-walled rectangular pipe and tube orders continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the antidumping orders on light-walled rectangular pipe and tube from China, Mexico, Korea and Türkiye and the countervailing duty order on China, applicable August 19, 2026.

changes.title: New investigations: welded stainless line and pressure pipe
changes.detail: Commerce opened antidumping investigations on welded stainless line and pressure pipe from India, Türkiye and the United Arab Emirates. No cash deposits apply until a preliminary determination. Welded stainless pressure pipe from China, India, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam is already under orders.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies: Section 232 goods exempt
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect. They do not apply to Section 232 goods (note 52(f)(1)), so in Chapter 73 they reach only the 14 cast-iron lines: cast-iron pipe, nonmalleable cast fittings, cast-iron radiators, cookware and baths. USMCA goods are exempt.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. It never applied to Section 232 goods (Proclamation 11012); in Chapter 73 it reached only the cast-iron lines outside Section 232, and not USMCA goods.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil: Section 232 goods exempt
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. Section 232 goods are excluded (note 50(a)(vi)(1)), so it reaches only the 14 cast-iron Chapter 73 lines, which also pay Brazil's 12.5% 2026 Section 301 rate.

changes.title: OCTG orders on China continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on oil country tubular goods (casing and tubing of 7304 and 7306) from China, applicable May 19, 2026. On February 27, 2026 it found that seamless OCTG completed in Thailand from Chinese billets circumvents these orders.

changes.title: Proclamation 11032: 85% test for U.S.-melted steel
changes.detail: From June 8, 2026, a derivative article qualifies for the 10% U.S.-melted rate (9903.82.06) when at least 85% of its steel (by weight) was melted and poured in the United States, instead of all of it. The proclamation also reset the rates on industrial and mobile equipment derivatives (Chapters 84 and 87); nothing else changed for Chapter 73.

changes.title: PC strand orders continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the antidumping orders on prestressed concrete steel wire strand (7312.10) from Brazil, India, Japan, Mexico, Korea and Thailand and the countervailing duty order on India, applicable June 2, 2026. The 2020 orders on 15 other countries passed their first sunset review in May 2026.
changes.countries: Brazil, India, Japan, Mexico, Korea, Thailand

changes.title: Taiwan: 15% auto parts rate
changes.detail: Under the U.S.–Taiwan trade and security agreement, passenger-vehicle parts of Taiwan pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.67) instead of +25%. In Chapter 73 this covers the leaf and coil springs for vehicles.

changes.title: Commerce corrects the Section 232 annex; Tata Steel UK clarified
changes.detail: Commerce added heading 9903.82.01 (articles on the lists with no steel, aluminum or copper pay no Section 232 duty) from April 6, 2026, and clarified that UK goods made by Tata Steel UK from steel melted and poured in the Netherlands may enter at the UK rates and count toward the 95% test until January 1, 2028.

changes.title: Commerce opens the 25% route for Canadian and Mexican pipe and tube
changes.detail: Under Proclamation 10984, Commerce set out how steel producers in Canada or Mexico that supply U.S. vehicle makers and commit to new U.S. steel capacity can apply for a reduced rate, not below 25%, on limited quantities. Approved steel articles of list (iii), which in Chapter 73 means sheet piling, rails and pipe and tube, enter under 9903.82.18 (+25%) if they qualify for USMCA and were melted and poured in Canada or Mexico. Derivative articles are not eligible.

changes.title: Section 232 rebuilt on full value: 50% or 25% (Proclamation 11021)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the earlier headings with 9903.82.02–9903.82.26, charged on the full customs value regardless of metal content. Chapter 73 steel articles and most derivatives stay at 50% (9903.82.02); the 64 household lines of list (vii) drop to 25% (9903.82.09). New lower rates: UK 25% / 15% with at least 95% UK-melted steel, and 10% for derivatives with U.S.-melted steel. The nonmalleable cast-iron articles of 7325.10 (manhole covers, catch basins, meter boxes) were added. Manufacturing drawback is allowed only for list (vii) goods of trade-agreement partners; goods entering a foreign-trade zone must take privileged foreign status. The derivatives inclusions process ended.

changes.title: Wind tower orders continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on utility scale wind towers (7308.20) from Canada, Vietnam, Indonesia and Korea, applicable March 16, 2026.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24, 2026. Section 232 duties are not IEEPA duties and continued unchanged. Since June 4, 2025 the IEEPA duties had not applied to Section 232 goods, so for Chapter 73 they had mattered mainly for the cast-iron lines.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs; Section 232 goods outside it
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026. Proclamation 11012 says it does not apply in addition to Section 232 duties, so Chapter 73 steel articles paid only Section 232; USMCA goods were exempt.

changes.title: Standard pipe finished in Oman from Chinese steel circumvents the China orders
changes.detail: Commerce found that circular welded carbon quality steel pipe (7306.30) completed in Oman from Chinese hot-rolled steel circumvents the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on China, which were continued in December 2024.

changes.title: OCTG orders on India, Korea, Türkiye, Vietnam and Ukraine: sunset findings
changes.detail: Commerce found that revoking the antidumping orders on oil country tubular goods from India, Korea, Türkiye, Vietnam and Ukraine would likely lead to continued dumping (second sunset reviews); the orders remain in place.

changes.title: Section 232 on medium- and heavy-duty truck parts
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 put 25% (9903.74.08) on parts of medium- and heavy-duty trucks and buses, including the leaf and coil springs of 7320.10 and 7320.20.10 used in them, in place of the metals duty. USMCA-qualifying parts are exempt (9903.74.10). It also authorized the 25% route for Canadian and Mexican steel (9903.82.18).

changes.title: South Korea: 15% auto parts rate
changes.detail: Passenger-vehicle parts of Korea pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.63) instead of +25%, including Chapter 73 vehicle springs.

changes.title: Japan: 15% auto parts rate
changes.detail: Passenger-vehicle parts of Japan pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.43) instead of +25%, including Chapter 73 vehicle springs.

changes.title: Cast and ductile fittings and other track material added to Section 232
changes.detail: Commerce's first inclusions round added ductile and other cast fittings (7307.19.30, 7307.19.90) and other railway track material (7302.90.90.00) to the Section 232 steel derivatives at 50%, and listed tubular towers (7308.20.00.35) as an aluminum derivative (200% when a Russian aluminum article).

changes.title: European Union: 15% auto parts rate
changes.detail: Passenger-vehicle parts of the EU pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.53) instead of +25%, including Chapter 73 vehicle springs.

changes.title: United Kingdom: 10% auto parts rate
changes.detail: Passenger-vehicle parts of the UK pay 10% (9903.94.32) instead of +25%, including Chapter 73 vehicle springs.

changes.title: Section 232 doubled to 50%
changes.detail: Proclamation 10947 raised the Section 232 steel duties, including on derivatives, from 25% to 50% for goods entered from 12:01 a.m. EDT on June 4, 2025, except for the UK (25%). It said the duty applies only to the steel content of Chapter 73 articles, with the non-steel content subject to the reciprocal tariff, and amended Executive Order 14289 so that Section 232 goods no longer paid the Canada and Mexico IEEPA duties. Drawback was ruled out.

changes.title: Section 232 on auto parts: vehicle springs
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 put 25% (9903.94.05) on automobile parts from May 3, 2025, including leaf and coil springs for passenger vehicles and light trucks (7320.10, 7320.20.10). Auto parts do not also pay the metals duty. USMCA-qualifying parts of Canada and Mexico stay exempt (9903.94.06) until Commerce sets a process for their non-U.S. content.

changes.title: Non-stacking order for Section 232, IEEPA and auto duties
changes.detail: Executive Order 14289, retroactive to March 4, 2025, set which duties stack: auto parts duties apply instead of the metals duty, and goods of Canada and Mexico subject to the IEEPA duties would not also pay Section 232 metals. Proclamation 10947 reversed the second rule from June 4, 2025.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff excludes Section 232 goods
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025 but excluded steel articles and derivatives subject to Section 232. In Chapter 73 it reached the cast-iron lines and, from June 4, 2025, the non-steel content of derivatives. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 extended to almost all Chapter 73 articles; all exemptions end
changes.detail: Proclamation 10896 restored the full 25% duty on steel from Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, Korea, the EU, Japan, the UK and Ukraine by ending their exemptions and quotas, stopped new product exclusions, and added the derivative steel articles of its Annex I. Commerce's annex (90 FR 11249) lists almost every other Chapter 73 provision: fittings, structures, containers, wire products, chain, nails, fasteners, springs, stoves, household and sanitary articles and other articles. For Chapter 73 derivatives the duty applied to the full value; for derivatives outside Chapter 73, only to the steel content.
changes.before: Pipe, tube, rails, sheet piling and some nails only

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA goods were exempted from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Country of melt and pour reported for steel imports
changes.detail: Importers must report the country where the steel was melted and poured on entries of Section 232 steel articles from all countries; from March 12, 2025 the field is mandatory in ACE for steel articles and derivatives, including Chapter 73 derivatives.

changes.title: China Section 301: steel pipe, tube and rails to 25%
changes.detail: After its four-year review, USTR moved Chinese steel and aluminum products to U.S. note 31 (9903.91.01) at 25%, including 79 Chapter 73 subheadings of pipe and tube, rails and sheet piling, from September 27, 2024.

changes.title: Mexico: 25% on steel not melted and poured in North America
changes.detail: Proclamation 10783 charged 25% on Mexican steel articles (including pipe and tube) melted and poured outside Mexico, Canada or the United States, while Mexican steel melted in North America stayed exempt. Superseded on March 12, 2025.

changes.title: EU, Japan and UK steel tariff-rate quotas
changes.detail: Proclamations 10328 (EU, from January 1, 2022), 10356 (Japan, April 1, 2022) and 10406 (UK, June 1, 2022) let steel articles such as pipe and tube, and derivatives such as nails, enter free of Section 232 duty within annual quotas. All ended March 12, 2025.

changes.title: First steel derivatives: nails, tacks and staples
changes.detail: Proclamation 9980 extended the 25% Section 232 duty to certain steel nails, tacks, staples and similar articles of 7317 (and bumper stampings of Chapter 87) from February 8, 2020, except from Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Mexico and Korea.

changes.title: Canada and Mexico exempted from Section 232 steel
changes.detail: Proclamation 9894 removed the Section 232 steel duty on Canada and Mexico from May 20, 2019. The exemption lasted until March 12, 2025.

changes.title: Section 232 extended to the EU, Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: Proclamation 9759 ended the temporary exemptions of the EU, Canada and Mexico on June 1, 2018 and set quotas for Argentina, Australia and Brazil.

changes.title: Section 232 steel tariff begins at 25%: pipe, tube, rails and sheet piling
changes.detail: Proclamation 9705 imposed a 25% duty on steel articles from March 23, 2018. In Chapter 73 its definition covered sheet piling (7301.10), rails and track material (7302.10, 7302.40–7302.90) and all pipe and tube of 7304–7306; other Chapter 73 articles were not covered.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 73 articles of iron or steel were **$44.20B in 2025**, -16.0% from $52.65B in 2024 (peak: $61.17B in 2022). The five largest suppliers were China ($9.27B), Mexico ($6.13B), Canada ($3.66B), Taiwan ($3.19B) and India ($2.93B). By product group the largest were structures and parts (7308, $7.45B), screws, bolts and nuts (7318, $6.43B) and other articles (7326, $5.94B); pipe and tube (7303–7306) totaled $7.44B, fittings (7307) $3.10B, stoves and grills (7321) $3.09B and household articles (7323) $2.78B.

2025 was the year Section 232 reached most of this chapter: on March 12 almost every Chapter 73 article became a steel derivative at 25%, and on June 4 the rate doubled to 50%. Imports from China fell 29.6% and from Canada 32.8%, while Vietnam rose 24.9% and India 3.3%. Household articles (7323) fell 35.1% and structures (7308) 19.8%; large welded pipe (7305) was one of the few groups that grew (+6.4%).

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. For most of Chapter 73 the answer is the same everywhere: **50%** on pipe and tube, fittings, structures, wire products, chain, nails, fasteners and springs, and **25%** on stoves, grills, radiators, kitchenware and sanitary ware, plus the base rate. Section 232 has no country exemptions and is collected on top of FTA and USMCA rates. China pays more (**75%** on pipe, nails, bolts and structures), Canadian 7308.90 structures pay **100%**, and the UK pays 25% or 15% with UK-melted steel (the cells show the default rates).

Differences between countries show up on the 14 cast-iron lines (2026 Section 301, Brazil and China duties, USMCA relief) and on vehicle springs, which pay the auto or truck parts duty: 15% for Japan, the EU, Korea and Taiwan, nothing for USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican parts. The table does **not** include antidumping or countervailing duties, which apply company by company to many pipe, fitting, fastener and wire imports (see Tariff updates).

rule.label: 75% on pipe, tube, rails, structures, nails, fasteners and most other steel articles: 50% Section 232 (9903.82.02) + 25% Section 301 (note 31, 9903.91.01, or Lists 2 and 3); 57.5% on List 4A pipe, nails, fasteners, needles and springs (7.5%). Stoves, grills and housewares of list (vii): 25% Section 232 plus 25% (List 3) or 7.5% (List 4A), or no Section 301 on the suspended List 4B lines (stainless cookware 27%). Cast-iron lines: List 3 25% plus 12.5% (9903.05.31). Vehicle springs pay the 25% auto or truck parts duty plus Section 301. Many Chinese pipe, fitting, nail, threaded rod, cylinder, sink and hanger products also carry AD/CVD, not shown.

50% (list (iii)–(iv)) or 25% (list (vii)) with or without a USMCA claim: Section 232 has applied to all Mexican steel goods since March 12, 2025 and is collected on top of the USMCA rate. Commerce can authorize limited quantities of Mexican pipe and tube at 25% (9903.82.18). The 14 cast-iron lines pay 10% Section 301 (9903.05.55) unless USMCA is claimed. USMCA-qualifying vehicle springs pay nothing (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10). Mexican rectangular tube, standard pipe and PC strand carry AD orders, not shown.

Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; KR for South Korea; JP for Japan. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): the China Section 301 product exclusions (9903.88.69), the 10% rate for derivatives with at least 85% U.S.-melted steel (9903.82.06), and the no-metal-content heading (9903.82.01).

Section 232 is shown at its default rates: 50% (9903.82.02) and 25% (9903.82.09). UK goods with at least 95% UK-melted steel pay 25% (9903.82.04) or 15% (9903.82.05), and Canadian or Mexican pipe and tube authorized by Commerce under 9903.82.18 pays 25%; the cells do not show these variants.

Vehicle springs (7320.10, 7320.20.10) show one total per use: auto-part (parts of passenger vehicles and light trucks, auto parts duty), truck-part (parts of medium- and heavy-duty trucks and buses, truck parts duty) and non-vehicle (metals duty); vehicle-part means the auto and truck rates are the same.
The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied.

Antidumping and countervailing duties are not included. They apply company by company to many Chapter 73 products: OCTG, line, standard, rectangular and stainless pipe, fittings, nails, threaded rod, wind towers, PC strand, propane cylinders, drawn stainless sinks, steel grating and garment hangers.
Entry rules apply to every Section 232 line: the country of melt and pour, and for pipe and tube a Commerce SIMA steel import license (19 CFR part 360; CBP CSMS 62582900).
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 2(aa), 16, 20, 29, 30, 31, 33, 38, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 73: Articles of Iron or Steel — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Steel Pipe, Fittings & Fasteners: Section 232 Entry, Melt-and-Pour, SIMA, Drawback & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 73) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 73 line: Section 232 entry (9903.82.02 or 9903.82.09), country of melt and pour, SIMA license for pipe and tube, mill certificates, FTZ status, marking, AD/CVD scope, plus the legal ways to pay less: U.S.- or UK-melted steel, correct classification, USMCA for cast iron, vehicle-part rates and drawback.
keywords: anti dumping duty on steel pipes from china

tariffEngineering.intro:
For Chapter 73 the Section 232 heading decides most of the duty. Every entry of a listed line reports **9903.82.02** (50%) or **9903.82.09** (25%) next to the Chapter 73 number, or the UK, U.S.-melted or Russia heading that replaces it, with the **country where the steel was melted and poured**; the duty is on the full value with no FTA reduction. Pipe and tube also need a **Commerce steel import license (SIMA)**, and the invoice must carry the mill analysis.

The legal ways to pay less: **steel melted and poured in the United States** (10% instead of 50% or 25% on derivatives), **UK-melted steel** (25% or 15%), Commerce-authorized Canadian or Mexican pipe and tube (25%), **avoiding Chinese origin** (Section 301), **classifying correctly** (cast-iron goods are outside Section 232; list (vii) goods pay 25%, not 50%), **USMCA** on the cast-iron lines and vehicle springs, the **vehicle-part rates** for springs, **drawback** on list (vii) goods from trade-agreement partners, and checking **AD/CVD scope** before you buy. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or proclamation.

levers.title: Use steel melted and poured in the United States
levers.saves: Most of the Section 232 duty on derivatives: 10% (9903.82.06) instead of 50% or 25% of the full value
levers.appliesTo: The 316 derivative lines of lists (iv) and (vii), all of Chapter 73 except pipe and tube, sheet piling and rails
levers.document: Mill certificates and supplier records showing that at least 85% of the steel content (by weight) was melted and poured in the United States, and ACE reporting of the melt-and-pour country (US).
levers.caveat: The 85% test applies from June 8, 2026 (before: all of the steel). Not available for list (iii) steel articles (pipe, tube, rails, sheet piling) or for Russian goods (9903.82.15 instead).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(e), heading 9903.82.06

levers.title: Buy UK goods made from UK-melted steel
levers.saves: Half the Section 232 duty or more: 25% (9903.82.04) instead of 50%, or 15% (9903.82.05) instead of 25%
levers.appliesTo: All Section 232 lines of Chapter 73, for products of the United Kingdom
levers.document: Mill certificates showing that at least 95% of the steel was melted and poured in the UK (Tata Steel UK steel melted in the Netherlands counts until January 1, 2028), and ACE reporting of the melt-and-pour country.
levers.caveat: Origin must be the UK and the 95% test must be met; otherwise 50% or 25%.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(d)
Commerce notice on Tata Steel UK (91 FR 23056)

levers.title: Canada or Mexico: the Commerce-authorized 25% rate for pipe and tube
levers.saves: Half the Section 232 duty (25% instead of 50%) on authorized quantities
levers.appliesTo: Sheet piling, rails and pipe and tube (list (iii)) of Canada or Mexico that qualify for USMCA and were melted and poured in Canada or Mexico
levers.document: Commerce authorization for the producer (submission under the April 23, 2026 procedures), USMCA certification of origin, and entry under heading 9903.82.18.
levers.caveat: Only for producers that supply U.S. automobile or heavy-vehicle makers and commit to new U.S. primary steel capacity, and only for the quantity Commerce sets. Derivative articles (fittings, structures, fasteners and the rest of Chapter 73) are not eligible.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(h), heading 9903.82.18

levers.title: Avoid Chinese origin
levers.saves: 25% of value on most lines: Chinese pipe, nails, bolts and structures pay 75% against 50% elsewhere
levers.appliesTo: 556 Chapter 73 lines carry a China Section 301 duty
levers.document: Production records showing where the article was made. Origin follows the last substantial transformation (for pipe and tube, the 19 CFR 102.20 rules for Chapter 73); ask CBP for a binding ruling when processing spans countries.
levers.caveat: Third-country finishing does not change Section 232 and can fall under AD/CVD circumvention findings: Commerce found in 2026 that OCTG finished in Thailand and standard pipe finished in Oman from Chinese steel, and garment hangers finished in Cambodia (preliminary), circumvent the China orders.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20 and 31

levers.title: Classify cast-iron and household goods correctly
levers.saves: The 50% Section 232 duty on the 14 cast-iron lines that are on no list, or 25 points on list (vii) goods that pay 25% instead of 50%
levers.document: Technical specifications: chemistry (cast iron under chapter note 1 is not steel), manufacturing method (cast, forged, welded, seamless), use; if unsure, a CBP binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Classification follows the product, not the duty, and misclassification is a penalty case. Cast-iron lines still pay the 2026 Section 301 duties for most countries, and Chinese cast-iron soil pipe and fittings carry AD/CVD.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(c)

levers.title: Vehicle springs: enter under the auto or truck parts heading
levers.saves: Leaf and coil springs for vehicles pay 25% (15% for Japan, the EU, Korea and Taiwan; 10% UK; nothing for USMCA-qualifying parts) instead of the 50% metals duty
levers.document: Evidence that the springs are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks (note 33) or of medium- or heavy-duty trucks or buses (note 38): customer, drawings, end use. USMCA certification for the Canada/Mexico exemption.
levers.caveat: Springs not for vehicles pay the metals duty. The auto parts rates depend on the country agreements and can change.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 33 and 38
CBP Section 232 FAQs: automobiles and parts

levers.title: Claim USMCA for cast-iron goods and vehicle springs
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty on Canadian and Mexican cast-iron pipe, fittings, radiators, cookware and baths, and the whole auto or truck parts duty on vehicle springs
levers.appliesTo: The 14 cast-iron lines and 6 vehicle-spring lines, for originating goods of Canada or Mexico
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer (no set format), available to CBP on request.
levers.caveat: A USMCA claim does not reduce Section 232 on any other Chapter 73 line (note 16(b)) or the Section 338 duty on Canadian 7308.90 structures. USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52

levers.title: Check AD/CVD scope before you buy
levers.saves: The whole antidumping or countervailing duty, when the product or producer is outside the order
levers.appliesTo: OCTG, line, standard, rectangular and stainless pipe, fittings, nails, threaded rod, wind towers, PC strand, propane cylinders, sinks, grating, garment hangers
levers.document: The order's written scope (it, not the HTS number, decides) and the producer's company-specific cash-deposit rate; when unsure, request a scope ruling from Commerce.

seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. tariffs on steel pipe, fittings, fasteners, nails, structures and housewares: the Section 232 derivatives list, how the 50% and 25% rates are calculated, Canada, Mexico, China and India, cookware, and HS codes for steel products.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs on articles of iron or steel: pipe and tube, fittings, structures, fasteners, nails, springs, stoves and housewares, by country and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: Almost all of Chapter 73 is under Section 232 on the full customs value, from every country and on top of any FTA or USMCA rate: 50% on 495 lines (pipe and tube, fittings, structures, wire products, chain, nails, fasteners, springs) and 25% on 64 household lines (stoves, grills, radiators, kitchenware, sinks). Only 14 cast-iron lines are outside it.

Chinese pipe, nails, bolts and structures pay 75% (Section 301 on top); Canadian 7308.90 structures pay 100% (Section 338 on top); UK goods with UK-melted steel pay 25% or 15%; derivatives with at least 85% U.S.-melted steel pay 10%. Vehicle springs pay the auto or truck parts duty instead.

The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026; the 2026 Section 301 duties skip Section 232 goods. Antidumping and countervailing duties on pipe, fittings, nails, threaded rod, wind towers and other products come on top and are not in the calculator.
In 2025 the U.S. imported $44.20B of Chapter 73 products, China ($9.27B) and Mexico ($6.13B) first.

faqs.question: What is the Section 232 steel derivative tariff, and what is on the list?
faqs.answer: Derivative steel articles are products made mostly of steel that Section 232 taxes like steel itself. Since April 6, 2026 the lists are in U.S. note 16(c) to Chapter 99: list (iv) (50%, heading 9903.82.02) and list (vii) (25%, 9903.82.09), plus derivative lists in other chapters. In Chapter 73, list (iv) covers fittings, structures, tanks, drums, gas cylinders, wire rope, mesh, chain, nails, fasteners, needles, springs and most cast and other articles; list (vii) covers stoves, grills, radiators, kitchenware, sinks and some wire articles. Pipe, tube, rails and sheet piling are steel articles (list (iii), 50%).

faqs.question: How is the steel derivative tariff calculated?
faqs.answer: For Chapter 73, multiply the full customs value by the Section 232 rate (50% or 25%) and add the base rate of the line and any other duty that stacks (China Section 301, Canada Section 338 on 7308.90). Since April 6, 2026 the duty is on the full value regardless of metal content (Proclamation 11021); the earlier steel-content basis no longer applies. FTA and USMCA claims do not reduce it. Report 9903.82.02 or 9903.82.09 with the Chapter 73 number and the country of melt and pour (CBP CSMS # 68253075).

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel pipe?
searchedAs: anti dumping duty on steel pipes from china
faqs.answer: Steel pipe and tube (HTS 7304 seamless, 7305 large welded, 7306 other welded) is Free under the general rate but pays the 50% Section 232 duty from every country (UK 25% with UK-melted steel; Commerce-authorized Canadian or Mexican quantities 25%). Chinese pipe pays 75% (25% Section 301 under note 31). Cast-iron pipe (7303) is outside Section 232. Many pipe products also carry AD/CVD orders: OCTG, line pipe, large-diameter welded pipe, standard pipe, rectangular tube and stainless pressure pipe.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel products from Canada?
faqs.answer: 50% on Canadian pipe, fittings, structures, fasteners, nails and other Chapter 73 steel articles, and 25% on stoves, grills, radiators and housewares, with or without a USMCA claim: Canada's Section 232 exemption ended March 12, 2025. Canadian structural parts, roofing and architectural work of 7308.90 pay another 50% under Section 338, 100% in total since September 15, 2026. USMCA still removes the 10% Section 301 duty on cast-iron goods and the auto parts duty on vehicle springs. Canada shipped $3.66B in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel products from Mexico?
searchedAs: us tariffs on steel from mexico
current tariffs on steel from mexico
is there a tariff on steel from mexico
faqs.answer: 50% (25% for stoves, grills, radiators and housewares) under Section 232, even with a USMCA certification: Mexico's exemption ended March 12, 2025. Mexican pipe and tube can get 25% only for Commerce-authorized quantities (9903.82.18). USMCA-qualifying Mexican vehicle springs pay no auto or truck parts duty, and cast-iron goods are Free with USMCA. Mexican rectangular tube, standard pipe and PC strand also carry AD orders. Mexico shipped $6.13B in 2025, mostly structures (7308) and other articles (7326).

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel products from China?
searchedAs: tariff on steel products from china
current tariff on steel products from china
us tariff on steel products from china
what is the tariff on steel from china
faqs.answer: 75% on Chinese pipe, tube, rails, structures, nails, fasteners and most other Chapter 73 steel articles: 50% Section 232 plus 25% Section 301 (note 31 or Lists 2 and 3); 57.5% on the List 4A pipe, nails, fasteners, needles and springs. Stoves, grills and housewares pay 25% Section 232 plus 25% or 7.5% Section 301; stainless cookware (7323.93) only 25% + its 2% base, because its Section 301 list never took effect. Cast-iron goods pay 25% + 12.5%. Many Chinese pipe, fitting, nail, threaded rod, cylinder, sink and hanger products also carry AD/CVD.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on steel products from India?
searchedAs: tariff on steel products from india
us tariff on steel products from india
faqs.answer: 50% Section 232 on Indian pipe, fittings, flanges, fasteners and other Chapter 73 steel articles, 25% on list (vii) household goods. India's 10% 2026 Section 301 duty applies only to the cast-iron lines, such as nonmalleable cast fittings (4.8% + 10%). Indian OCTG, large-diameter welded pipe, welded pipe, forged fittings, threaded rod, PC strand and stainless pressure pipe also carry AD/CVD orders. India shipped $2.93B in 2025, the most in fittings (7307).

faqs.question: What is the tariff and HS code for bolts, screws and nuts?
searchedAs: hs code for bolts and nuts
hs code for bolts washers nuts
faqs.answer: Steel fasteners are in heading 7318: screws and bolts 7318.11–7318.15, nuts 7318.16, washers 7318.21–7318.22, rivets and pins 7318.23–7318.24. Base rates run from Free (most bolts and nuts) to 12.5% (coach screws and wood screws), and every line pays the 50% Section 232 duty, so bolts from Taiwan, Japan or Germany pay 50% to 62.5% in total and Chinese fasteners 57.5% to 87.5% (75% plus the base rate on most). Threaded rod from China, India, Taiwan and Thailand also carries AD/CVD.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on steel nails?
faqs.answer: Yes. Steel nails, tacks and staples (heading 7317) are Free at base but pay the 50% Section 232 duty from every country (some nails have been under Section 232 since February 8, 2020); Chinese nails pay 75%. Nails from China, the UAE, Korea, Malaysia, Oman, Taiwan and Vietnam also carry antidumping orders, confirmed in 2025 and 2026 sunset reviews.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on steel cookware and kitchenware?
faqs.answer: Yes. Steel and stainless kitchenware (7323.93, 7323.94, 7323.99) is on Section 232 list (vii): 25% of the full value from every country, plus the 2% to 8.2% base rate, so stainless cookware pays 27%. From China it is still 27% (no Section 301 on 7323.93). Cast-iron skillets and pots (7323.91, 7323.92) are outside Section 232 and pay their base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%) for most countries.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on structural steel and steel structures?
faqs.answer: Steel structures and parts (heading 7308: bridges, towers, doors and windows, scaffolding, grating, other structural parts) are Free at base and pay the 50% Section 232 duty from every country. Canadian 7308.90.30, 7308.90.60 and 7308.90.95 goods pay 100% (Section 338 on top since September 15, 2026); Chinese structures 75%. Wind towers from Canada, Indonesia, Korea and Vietnam and steel grating from China carry AD/CVD. 7308 was the largest Chapter 73 import in 2025 ($7.45B).

faqs.question: Does USMCA exempt steel products from the Section 232 tariff?
faqs.answer: No. U.S. note 16(b) to Chapter 99 says the Section 232 duty is collected on top of any FTA or USMCA rate, so USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican Chapter 73 goods pay 50% or 25%. A USMCA claim still removes the 10% Section 301 duty on the 14 cast-iron lines and the auto or truck parts duty on vehicle springs. Commerce can authorize limited quantities of Canadian or Mexican pipe and tube at 25%.

faqs.question: Are the steel tariffs still in effect?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on steel
are there still tariffs on steel
is there still a tariff on steel
faqs.answer: Yes. The Section 232 duties on Chapter 73 steel articles and derivatives are in the current tariff schedule (2026 Revision 21): 50% since June 4, 2025 (Proclamation 10947), on the full value at 50% or 25% since April 6, 2026 (Proclamation 11021). The Supreme Court's February 20, 2026 ruling in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump ended only the IEEPA tariffs; the steel tariffs rest on Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and were not affected.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for steel pipe and other steel products?
searchedAs: hs code for steel pipe fittings
hs code for stainless steel pipe
faqs.answer: Steel articles are in HTS Chapter 73: cast-iron pipe 7303, seamless pipe and tube 7304, large welded pipe 7305, other welded pipe and tube (including galvanized, square and stainless) 7306, pipe fittings 7307, structures 7308, tanks and containers 7309–7311, wire rope 7312, mesh and fencing 7314, chain 7315, nails 7317, bolts, screws and nuts 7318, springs 7320, stoves and grills 7321, kitchenware 7323, sinks 7324, and other articles 7326 (7326.90 for most other steel articles, 7326.20 for wire articles). Steel sheet, bars and wire themselves are in Chapter 72. Use the rate table to search by product name.
